title: La femme du site  (The Woman from the Website)

segments.t: She has: a few nights ago, on a dating website, Andréa chatted with a woman and ended the chat with a very rude message. That woman was Colette. We'll hear the scene in French first. Don't worry about every word; the looks between them say a lot. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
C'est dingue! Je vous ai vue quelque part.
Je vais vous donner un indice.
Je cite: pas de petites filles comme vous.
Oh non. C'était vous!
Laissez-moi tranquille!
C'était juste un malentendu.
Colette, on a raté notre premier rendez-vous.
Laissez la porte ouverte, s'il vous plaît.
Vous êtes bien plus jolie en vrai.
Maintenant vous êtes gentille, à cause de votre agence.
C'est pathétique.
Pas du tout. Je suis sincère.
Je ne mélange pas le travail et la vie privée.
Je veux juste parler.
On peut en rire?
Moi, je n'ai pas envie de rire.
Partez maintenant. Au revoir, madame Martel.
Au revoir, Colette.
Let's go back through it. Andréa starts with a smile, trying to place the face.
C'est dingue!
'It's crazy!' The last word is casual, the kind of thing you say to a friend.
Je vous ai vue quelque part.

'I've seen you somewhere.' Here's this scene's first language point. Andréa uses the polite 'you' with Colette, and she keeps it all the way through, even while flirting. Colette is a stranger, and she's here on official business.
Je vais vous donner un indice.
'I'll give you a clue.' The verb 'to go' plus another verb: the near future. Colette has been waiting for this moment.
Je cite: pas de petites filles comme vous.
'I quote: no little girls like you.' She quotes Andréa's own rude message from the dating site, toned down here.
Oh non. C'était vous!
'Oh no. It was you!' The verb is in the past: 'it was'. Now Andréa understands.
Laissez-moi tranquille!
'Leave me alone!' A polite command, ending in the sound of the polite 'you'. The little word for 'me' is attached after it with a hyphen. Andréa tries to explain.
C'était juste un malentendu.
'It was just a misunderstanding.' A long word, but you can almost see the English in it: 'mis-heard'. Then she tries charm.
Colette, on a raté notre premier rendez-vous.
'Colette, we missed our first date.' The small word for 'we' at the start is the everyday one.
Laissez la porte ouverte, s'il vous plaît.
'Leave the door open, please.' She doesn't want to be alone in a closed room with Andréa. The last part is the polite 'please', literally 'if it pleases you'.
Vous êtes bien plus jolie en vrai.
'You're much prettier in real life.' The word for 'pretty' takes a feminine ending here. Colette isn't fooled.
Maintenant vous êtes gentille, à cause de votre agence.
'Now you're being nice, because of your agency.' The word for 'nice' is feminine too, because Andréa is a woman. Colette thinks she's only nice because of the tax audit.
C'est pathétique.
'It's pathetic.' Easy to guess from the English.
Pas du tout. Je suis sincère.
'Not at all. I mean it.' The second sentence literally says 'I am sincere'. Colette lays down her rule.
Je ne mélange pas le travail et la vie privée.
'I don't mix work and private life.' Another grammar point: to make a verb negative, French wraps two little words around it, one before, one after. Andréa insists.
Je veux juste parler.
'I just want to talk.' The verb 'to want' plus another verb in its basic form.
On peut en rire?
'Can we laugh about it?' The little word in the middle means 'about it'. Colette is not amused.
Moi, je n'ai pas envie de rire.
'I don't feel like laughing.' Literally 'I don't have the desire to laugh'. The negative wraps around 'have'.
Partez maintenant. Au revoir, madame Martel.
'Leave now. Goodbye, Ms Martel.' Another polite command, and her surname: very cold, very official. Andréa answers with her first name.
Au revoir, Colette.
'Goodbye, Colette.' Using the first name is Andréa's last little attempt at warmth. Let's listen to the whole scene again.
C'est dingue! Je vous ai vue quelque part.
Je vais vous donner un indice.
Je cite: pas de petites filles comme vous.
Oh non. C'était vous!
Laissez-moi tranquille!
C'était juste un malentendu.
Colette, on a raté notre premier rendez-vous.
Laissez la porte ouverte, s'il vous plaît.
Vous êtes bien plus jolie en vrai.
Maintenant vous êtes gentille, à cause de votre agence.
C'est pathétique.
Pas du tout. Je suis sincère.
Je ne mélange pas le travail et la vie privée.
Je veux juste parler.
On peut en rire?
Moi, je n'ai pas envie de rire.
Partez maintenant. Au revoir, madame Martel.
Au revoir, Colette.
A very awkward meeting, and not the last one between these two. Notice how the polite 'you' keeps a cool distance between them the whole time. See you next time!
À bientôt!
